hook.text: The trio had no set approach beyond looking for unique moments in the music and capturing them.

sentences.text: The Pearl is the pair's second album together, after Ambient 2: The Plateaux of Mirror (1980).
Like Ambient 2, it is built mostly from subtly treated piano textures, with noticeable electronic treatments and recordings of nature added.
Budd says the two albums are alike in sound and timbre, and that the likeness was there from the start of production.
Ambient 2 came together effortlessly, and the duo believed they could make similar music again without much trouble.
Budd said The Pearl was harder to make. He put this down to the duo's naivety on Ambient 2, and to a musical language that had matured since.
For the length of the sessions, the three stayed in one house and worked seven days a week.
Recording took two weeks, and finishing the record took 8 to 12 months, as they worked out which pieces suited each other.
Eno made most of the aesthetic calls and spent hours working alone, recording pieces at varied speeds.
Among the pianos were an acoustic one and electric models by Yamaha and Rhodes.
The treatments came from gear that included a Yamaha DX7, a Sequential Circuits Pro One, an AMS digital delay and an Eventide Harmonizer.

listen_for.text: Budd improvises over humming tones that Eno plays on a Yamaha CS-80, in a single take.
Budd laid it down first at a small studio, and Eno then reworked it, which Budd calls an extreme version of how the pair worked.
